note: Thesis: reopening the Strait of Hormuz brings an observable recovery in actual transits and, through recovering Middle East crude supply, lower front-month Brent prices. Stance is relative to this thesis: supports = backs a link in the chain (formal opening notices, oil prices falling on reopening, prices easing once flow constraints resolve, analogs of traffic recovering); contradicts = weakens it (transits not recovering or quickly reversing after announced openings or ceasefires, insurers and carriers not following, alternative bypass supply, oil prices driven by bypass-route attacks and risk premiums); neutral = background only (geography, historical flows and transit baselines, PortWatch measurement method, release cadence and revisions). 2026 timeline per the excerpts: 4/8 ceasefire, 6/17 MoU, 6/20 JMIC 'open' notice, 7/12 IRGC re-closure; PortWatch daily data through 2026-10-11, EIA STEO through 2026-10-06. Pre-closure baselines (hz-009, hz-020) are historical values, not a recovery threshold: what level counts as recovery must still be confirmed by the user.

excerpts.source: EIA Today in Energy, 2025-06-16 (T1 official data) · opening paragraph
excerpts.text: The Strait of Hormuz, located between Oman and Iran, connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

excerpts.source: EIA Today in Energy, 2025-06-16 (T1 official data) · opening paragraph
excerpts.text: In 2024, oil flow through the strait averaged 20 million barrels per day (b/d), or the equivalent of about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption.

excerpts.source: EIA Today in Energy, 2025-06-16 (T1 official data) · bypass pipelines paragraph
excerpts.text: The pipelines do not typically operate at full capacity, and we estimate that about 2.6 million b/d of capacity from the Saudi and UAE pipelines could be available to bypass the Strait of Hormuz in the event of a supply disruption.

excerpts.source: JMIC Advisory Note 010-26, 'Strait of Hormuz Open' (T1 official) · section 1
excerpts.text: The maritime security threat level in the SoH remains MODERATE following the announced intentions by both the United States and Iran for an opening of the waterway. However, Mariners should be advised of the existence of mines and expect naval presence as clearance operations continue.

excerpts.source: IMF PortWatch Daily Chokepoints Data (T1 official data) · portname='Strait of Hormuz', n_total, 2025 and 2026-02-15 to 02-27
excerpts.text: PortWatch daily transit counts for the Strait of Hormuz averaged about 85.5 vessels per day in 2025 and about 92 per day from 2026-02-15 to 2026-02-27, before the closure.

excerpts.source: IMF PortWatch Daily Chokepoints Data (T1 official data) · portname='Strait of Hormuz', n_total, 2026-04-09 to 04-28
excerpts.text: After the ceasefire announced on 2026-04-08, PortWatch daily transits through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about 6.3 vessels from 2026-04-09 to 04-28, with a maximum of 20.

excerpts.source: IMF PortWatch Daily Chokepoints Data (T1 official data) · portname='Strait of Hormuz', n_total, 2026-06-17 to 07-08
excerpts.text: After the US-Iran MoU of 2026-06-17 and the JMIC 'open' notice of 06-20, PortWatch daily transits averaged about 24 vessels from 06-18 to 07-08, peaking at 51 on 06-24, under half the pre-closure level.

excerpts.source: Reuters (T2 wire, via internazionale.it reprint) · lead
excerpts.text: July 12 (Reuters) - Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said early on Sunday it had closed the Strait of Hormuz until further notice after firing a warning shot at a vessel it said had attempted to transit along an unapproved route, state media reported.

excerpts.source: IMF PortWatch Daily Chokepoints Data (T1 official data) · portname='Strait of Hormuz', n_total, 2026-07-09 to 10-11
excerpts.text: PortWatch daily transits through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about 5.4 vessels from 2026-07-09 to 07-31 and about 3.7 from 08-26 to 10-11, with a maximum of 8 (data through 2026-10-11).

excerpts.source: Insurance Business (T3 trade media) · lede and Joint War Committee section
excerpts.text: President Trump's claim that the US Navy has removed or detonated all mines in the Strait of Hormuz changes the kinetic picture, but it does not change the insurance one, at least not yet. … That listing will not be removed until the committee sees sustained incident-free passage, a settled geopolitical picture, and formal evidence that demining is complete.

excerpts.source: IMF PortWatch Daily Chokepoints Data (T1 official data) · portname='Bab el-Mandeb Strait', n_total
excerpts.text: Historical counterexample: PortWatch daily transits through Bab el-Mandeb averaged about 78 vessels before the Houthi attacks (2023-10-01 to 11-14), about 32 after the 2025-01-19 Gaza ceasefire and about 34 after the 2025-05-06 US-Houthi ceasefire.

excerpts.source: Reuters (T2 wire, via Arab News reprint) · carrier statements
excerpts.text: "We will closely analyze the latest developments and their impact on the security situation in the Red Sea," said a Hapag-Lloyd spokesperson. "It is still too early to speculate about timing," a Maersk spokesperson said.

excerpts.source: Reuters (T2 wire, via ESM Magazine reprint) · body
excerpts.text: Ukrainian transport authorities last week said 91 vessels exported 3.3 million metric tonnes of agricultural and metal products as of 9 November.

excerpts.source: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026 (T1 official data) · PDF p.6 'Global oil prices'
excerpts.text: Following the signing in June of the memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran, the spot price of Brent crude oil fell as low as $69 per barrel (b) on July 2. Global crude oil prices rose and volatility increased later in July following renewed attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the related reduction in oil shipments through the waterway.

excerpts.source: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026 (T1 official data) · PDF p.6
excerpts.text: We estimate that crude oil and petroleum liquids transported through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 4.9 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), down from an average of 21.6 million b/d in 4Q25 before the conflict began.

excerpts.source: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026 (T1 official data) · PDF pp.6-7
excerpts.text: We forecast the Brent crude oil spot price will average $105/b in the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q26), $14/b higher than in last month's STEO. … we forecast that oil prices will remain elevated until constraints on oil flows from the Middle East resolve and oil inventories can be replenished.

excerpts.source: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026 (T1 official data) · PDF p.6
excerpts.text: The Brent crude oil spot price increased to an average of $114 per barrel (b) in September, $23/b higher than in August. … The most notable among these developments were attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, which temporarily halted flows on a crucial bypass used to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz.

excerpts.source: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026 (T1 official data) · PDF p.7
excerpts.text: The heightened risk associated with oil tankers transiting the region has added to shipping costs and increased the risk premium reflected in oil prices. High tanker rates, which reached record levels in September, reflect increasing insurance costs and are putting additional upward pressure on delivered crude oil prices to refiners.
